title: Canonical URL broken on all pages — always points to /
description: Every page renders <link rel="canonical" href="https://voxpelli.com/"> regardless of actual URL. Root cause: DomStack doesn't pass pageUrl to layouts for directly-rendered pages. vars.pageUrl is empty/falsy, defaults to '/'. See domstack-issues/12-pageurl-not-available-in-layouts.md. Harms SEO and IndieWeb URL discovery.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Article pages have correct canonical URL matching their path
- [ ] u-url/u-uid hrefs are non-empty on post footers
- [ ] Webmention form target includes page path, not just siteUrl
close_reason: Fixed: layouts now destructure page param from DomStack and derive pageUrl from page.path. Canonical URLs, OG URLs, webmention targets all correct.

title: XSS hardening pass — escape tag name + encode postUrl before rawHtml
description:
Two instances of the template-literal-into-rawHtml bypass pattern (see BM note XSS in Template Literal Contexts). (1) tags.template.js lines 68 and 73 interpolate tag name raw into children HTML and vars.title — if a tag ever contains <">&, both the page body and <title> break or inject. Use escapeXml from src/lib/escape.js. (2) renderExcerpt in src/lib/render-post.js around line 100-106 interpolates postUrl unescaped into <a href> then wraps in rawHtml. Currently trusted but pattern invites future bugs. Either rewrite renderExcerpt using html tagged template, or run postUrl through encodeURI.



## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create a test post with tag value containing HTML, e.g. `<script>alert(1)</script>`.
2. Build and inspect rendered tag markup.
3. Observe unescaped HTML interpolated into the page.
4. Similarly pass a javascript: URL via postUrl and observe it reaching rawHtml() unencoded.
acceptance_criteria: Tag names HTML-escaped before interpolation; postUrl encoded via encodeURIComponent before rawHtml; regression test covers <script>-bearing tag and javascript: postUrl

title: Service Worker hardening — clients.claim + cache warming + offline fallback
description:
sw.js has two related issues surfaced in the client-JS review: (1) activate event missing self.clients.claim(), so a newly-installed SW does not control already-open tabs until reload — first install = no SW behavior; (2) fetch handler is pure network-first and never calls cache.put on successful responses — only pre-cached URLs available offline, any runtime-visited page is offline-unavailable. Fix: add skipWaiting() in install, clients.claim() in activate (with old-cache cleanup), runtime cache.put with response.clone() in fetch handler (only for res.ok, HTML resources), caches.match(OFFLINE_FALLBACK_URL) on fetch failure. See BM note engineering/frontend/service-worker-fetch-strategies-offline-without-accidentally-going-offline-only for full pattern.



## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open DevTools → Application → Service Worker on a fresh profile.
2. Load the site once to register sw.js.
3. Inspect Cache Storage — note shell assets absent until first fetch.
4. Go offline, reload — no offline fallback served for navigation requests.
acceptance_criteria: sw.js activate calls clients.claim(); install event warms the cache with core shell assets; offline fallback HTML served for failed navigation requests; smoke/E2E coverage added

title: FOWT inline script broken — htm entity-encodes inside <script> tag
description: The FOWT prevention script added in root.layout.js is inside an html tagged template from async-htm-to-string. htm HTML-encodes apostrophes and ampersands inside script content, producing ' and & which break the JS. title: Adopt DomStack upstream PRs #240–#253 post-merge
description:
Fires when a DomStack release containing the 13 currently-open upstream PRs (bcomnes/domstack#240–#253) is published to npm. Migrates voxpelli.com off current workarounds and onto the upstream-provided primitives.

Seven PRs introduce behavior changes the site must adopt; six are docs-only with no required file changes.

## Sequencing (4 children)
1. Children 1 + 2 share files (feeds.template.js, tags.template.js) — MUST be one commit
2. Child 4 fully independent, can ship day 1
3. Child 3 highest risk (canonical URL regressions invisible without assertions) — last, with new smoke tests in same commit

## Rollback strategy
Pin @domstack/static to exact release SHA during migration. If new release regresses, revert the pin. filterAndSortPosts helper stays in codebase until deliberately removed in child issues, so pin-revert fully restores prior behaviour.

## External gate
Depends on a DomStack release containing all 13 PRs being published to npm. Not tracked as a beads dep because the release is external; monitor bcomnes/domstack#248 for status.

## Acceptance
- All four child issues closed
- npm test passes on the release version
- No filterAndSortPosts import in feeds.template.js
- No local PageData typedef in global.data.js
- npm run e2e canonical URL assertions pass (added in child 3)
acceptance_criteria: All 4 children closed; tests + e2e green on new release; workarounds removed per child-issue acceptance criteria

title: Focus-visible audit — skip-link, theme-toggle, hamburger
description:
Group issue covering three focus-ring issues across different elements. One coherent keyboard-accessibility pass beats three ad-hoc fixes.

## Scope
- .skip-link uses :focus (not :focus-visible) — asymmetric outline semantics
- <theme-toggle> Shadow DOM lacks :focus-visible rule — ring invisible to keyboard users inside Shadow DOM isolation
- Hamburger focus ring contrast 4.3:1 in dark mode — borderline WCAG AA

## Rationale
All three are focus-ring failures with different root causes (cascade, shadow-DOM isolation, color contrast). Auditing together surfaces the pattern and prevents future regressions.

## Children
- voxpelli.github.com-9wr — .skip-link :focus-visible
- voxpelli.github.com-y6t — <theme-toggle> Shadow DOM :focus-visible
- voxpelli.github.com-2sp — hamburger WCAG contrast

## Acceptance
All three keyboard-focus ring issues resolved; add an E2E test that tabs through keyboard-reachable controls and asserts visible focus ring at each stop in both themes.
acceptance_criteria: All children closed; keyboard focus ring visible on every reachable control in both themes; E2E tab-through test added

title: Launch /til/ section — TIL practice + community hook + Bluesky POSSE-reverse seed
description:
Add a /til/ section that gives TIL-shape content (currently scattered across Bluesky #TIL, essay-length commit bodies, and Raindrop AI-bookmarked curator notes) a canonical home on voxpelli.com and hooks into the Willison-TIL community (simonw/til, jvns.ca/til, thoughtbot/til).

## Why
Blog silent 2019-2026 due to platform debt (now fixed). TIL-shape content is being written in three other places. A /til/ section is a publishing target for existing writing habits — not a new habit to form.

## Design decisions (from research this session)
- URL: /til/YYYY/MM/<slug>/ — date-clustered. DomStack pins URL=directory (@domstack/static/lib/identify-pages.js:319 hardcodes path=dir, no permalink override). Dates are immutable; topic-as-URL would bake mutable taxonomy into permanent URLs.
- Topic discovery: frontmatter 'topic' or TIL-scoped tags rendered at /til/topics/<name>/. Kept separate from /tags/ (existing vocabulary is essay-meta and would muddy both corpora — only ~32 posts tagged in 15yr).
- Post kind: h-entry with category:til; mf-bookmark-of optional (sparked-by-reading TILs cite, pure authored tricks don't).
- Seed: 3 Bluesky #TIL POSSE-reversals, origin-dated with via: link. NOT back-dated-pretending. Plus launch meta-post on main blog. No Raindrop-lift at launch — AI-bookmarked items are durably hosted, lifting is retcon not rescue.
- /links/ frozen, not replaced — 14 posts, 0% link rot, 70% mini-essays. Coexistence beats collapse (adactio.com, macwright.com precedent).
- Community hooks: /til/ URL prefix + #TIL POSSE to Bluesky + /til/feed.atom + webmentions on source citations.

## Out of scope (deferred / separate issues)
- u-revises microformat MVP on pre-2019 archive
- Raindrop-lift helper automation
- Bluesky #TIL auto-harvest cron
acceptance_criteria: /til/ section live with topic discovery, separate Atom feed, 3 seed posts, launch meta-post on main blog, /til/ in site navigation

title: sitemap.xml includes redirects, feeds, 404 — SEO waste
description:
src/sitemap.xml.template.js enumerates every page DomStack knows about, including meta-refresh redirect stubs from redirects.template.js and the 404 page. Search engines will crawl and try to index the redirect stubs, potentially surfacing them instead of canonical targets. Fix: filter the pages array before building URL list — exclude paths matching redirect 'from' paths, paths ending in .xml, the /404/ path.



## Steps to Reproduce
1. npm run build.
2. Inspect public/sitemap.xml — redirect pages from redirects.template.js appear as entries.
3. Also observe /all.xml, /links/all.xml, /offline/, /404/ listed as indexable URLs.
4. SEO impact: crawlers waste budget on non-canonical pages.
acceptance_criteria: /sitemap.xml excludes redirect pages, feed files (*.xml), and 404.html; only canonical content URLs listed; smoke test asserts the exclusions

title: <relative-time> connectedCallback not idempotent — double-appends on reconnect
description:
src/global.client.js RelativeTime connectedCallback (~lines 131-145) appends a '.relative-label' span to the <time> without a guard. If the element is moved in the DOM (View Transition swap, framework re-render, any adoptNode/moveBefore), the callback fires again and the page shows '(2 days ago) (2 days ago)'. Low risk in normal MPA navigation, but the pattern is wrong. Fix: add 'if (this.querySelector(".relative-label")) return;' at top, or remove any pre-existing span before appending. See BM One-Shot State Antipattern subtype 1 (lifecycle-callback idempotency).



## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create a <relative-time><time datetime="2020-01-01"></time></relative-time>.
2. Call element.remove() then document.body.appendChild(element).
3. Inspect shadow/light DOM — two .relative-label spans present instead of one.
4. Each subsequent reconnect appends another label.
acceptance_criteria: connectedCallback idempotent — guards against duplicate append; a single .relative-label span exists regardless of reconnect count; regression test covers detach/reattach cycle

title: <theme-toggle> Shadow DOM has no :focus-visible rule — broken focus ring
description:
The theme-toggle web component's Shadow DOM <style> block (src/global.client.js TOGGLE_STYLES ~lines 24-66) defines button:hover opacity but has no button:focus-visible rule. The site's outer focus-visible rule cannot penetrate the shadow boundary. Keyboard users tabbing through the theme toggle see no focus ring — WCAG 2.4.11 (Focus Appearance) failure. Fix: add 'button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid currentColor; outline-offset: 2px; }' to TOGGLE_STYLES. See BM note Shadow DOM Theming → Accessibility Across the Shadow Boundary.



## Steps to Reproduce
1. Load site with keyboard focus starting on body.
2. Tab until focus lands on one of the three <theme-toggle> buttons.
3. Observe no visible focus ring — default UA ring was suppressed by button:focus { outline: none } inside Shadow DOM.
4. Shadow DOM isolation means outer :focus-visible rules do not reach.
acceptance_criteria: Shadow DOM <style> block inside <theme-toggle> includes a :focus-visible rule that matches the outer site's focus-ring convention; keyboard tab through buttons shows a visible ring

title: Atom feed correctness — stable <id> and add <published>
description:
Two Atom spec issues in src/lib/render-rss-entry.js: (1) entry <id> = siteUrl + post.pageUrl collapses to just siteUrl when pageUrl is empty — readers use <id> to dedupe, so all empty-pageUrl entries merge into one. Guard with explicit check or synthetic tag URI. (2) Emits <updated> but no <published>. Without <published>, readers can't distinguish 'first posted' from 'last edited' — typo fixes later have no way to bump <updated> semantically. Emit both, seeded equal at publish time. See BM note RSS and Feed Syndication section on timestamp semantics.



## Steps to Reproduce
1. npm run build.
2. Open public/all.xml. Observe <id> duplicates the <link href>.
3. Note absence of <published> — only <updated> is present; readers cannot distinguish original vs edited dates.
4. Paste the feed into https://validator.w3.org/feed/ — flags these issues.
acceptance_criteria: <id> is a stable tag: URI (RFC 4151) independent of URL changes; <published> emitted alongside <updated>; W3C feed validator reports no errors on /all.xml, /english.xml, /links/all.xml, /til/feed.atom

title: System theme mode does not follow OS prefers-color-scheme changes live
description: applyTheme and the inline pre-paint script read matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme:dark)') once and write data-theme unconditionally, defeating the CSS @media fallback. When macOS auto-switches at sunset the page stays stuck. Fix: platform-native approach — omit data-theme when mode is system, let CSS @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) :root:not([data-theme]) handle the response.

title: Nav scroll lock leaks when resizing mobile→desktop with drawer open
description: body.style.overflow='hidden' stays stuck on desktop because setNavOpen's isMobile() gate skips the clear branch when the MQ change listener fires past the breakpoint. WCAG 1.4.10 regression. Fix: make overflow lock unconditional on the (open && isMobile()) expression.

title: Retarget syntax highlighting CSS from Rouge to highlight.js classes
description: The 28+ syntax highlighting rules in global.css use Jekyll/Rouge class conventions (.highlight .c, .highlight .k, .highlight .err) but DomStack renders with highlight.js classes (.hljs .hljs-attr, .hljs .hljs-string). The entire theme is dead CSS. Retarget to .hljs token classes or use a highlight.js CSS theme file. The dark mode color tokens (--hl-bg, --hl-comment, etc.) are already defined — just the selectors need updating.
close_reason: Replaced 28 dead Rouge/Jekyll selectors with 18 working highlight.js selectors targeting actual built output classes

title: Button 3D shadow invisible in dark mode
description:
box-shadow: 4px 4px 0 var(--color-stone) disappears in dark mode — stone color nearly identical to canvas. Introduce --color-btn-shadow token that resolves to stone in light mode and a visible value in dark mode. Also deduplicate the two identical .btn rule blocks in global.css.



## Steps to Reproduce
1. Toggle dark mode via <theme-toggle> or OS preference.
2. Hover or focus a primary button (e.g. submit button on webmention form, theme-toggle active state).
3. Observe 3D offset shadow is invisible — shadow color blends with dark canvas-alt background.
4. Contrast check: box-shadow color too close to surrounding surface in dark palette.
acceptance_criteria: Button 3D offset shadow visible in dark mode with sufficient contrast against --color-canvas-alt; dark-mode-specific box-shadow color or increased offset ensures visibility
notes:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Visit site in dark mode (toggle via theme switcher or OS preference)
2. Focus or hover any button (e.g. theme-toggle buttons, form submit)
3. Observe 3D offset shadow

## Expected
Shadow visible with adequate contrast against dark canvas.

## Actual
Shadow blends into background / invisible.

title: iOS Safari safe area insets for fixed elements
description:
Fixed-position elements (reading progress bar, hamburger overlay) jump on iOS Safari when address bar collapses. Add viewport-fit=cover to meta tag in root.layout.js. Add env(safe-area-inset-bottom) padding to relevant fixed elements. Thumb-zone research documented in BM note.



## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open site on iPhone with notch (iPhone X+) in portrait.
2. Open hamburger drawer — bottom of drawer overlapped by home-indicator.
3. Rotate to landscape — drawer/nav clipped under the notch on the left.
4. No env(safe-area-inset-*) present in CSS for fixed elements.
acceptance_criteria: env(safe-area-inset-*) applied to fixed/sticky elements (hamburger, drawer, any bottom-pinned UI); portrait + landscape respected on notched iOS devices; no content obscured by home-indicator or notch

Follow existing pattern in e2e/sidebar.test.js.

If this page renders without horizontal scroll at 375px, all real content works.

title: markdown-it.settings.js — structural wrappers for rich content
description: Create src/markdown-it.settings.js with render rules: html_block wraps bare <iframe> in div.video-embed, image wraps titled images in figure/figcaption, fence wraps code blocks in div.code-block, table_open/table_close wraps tables in div.table-wrapper. Add matching CSS for all wrapper classes. Zero new dependencies. DomStack convention: export default async function(md) { return md }. See Content Architecture BM note for rationale (newsdoc thinking applied to markdown).
design: Four markdown-it renderer rule overrides applied at build time. Source stays plain markdown. Wrappers are purely additive — an unstyled iframe still embeds. CSS classes: .video-embed (aspect-ratio: 16/9), .code-block (overflow-x: auto), .table-wrapper (overflow-x: auto), figure/figcaption.
acceptance_criteria: Markdown output wraps code blocks/tables/figures with semantic containers per settings; existing published posts render visually unchanged; smoke tests pass

title: Fix null-safety type error in RelativeTime web component
description: The new browser tsconfig (arc) caught a type error at src/global.client.js:135 — getAttribute('datetime') can return null. The querySelector('time[datetime]') guarantees the attribute exists at runtime, but tsc cannot infer that. Fix: add a null guard or non-null assertion.

title: Unify social page like renderer with render-post-like.js

title: Add extractFullDomain utility and fix extractName TLD handling

For displaying liked/replied-to URLs as readable domain names, we need extractFullDomain() that returns the full registrable domain. Uses new URL() which is available in Node 20+.

Graceful fallback for malformed URLs

title: Print rule ordering trap — a::after suppression scope
description: src/global.css:1762-1773 inside @media print: line 1762 'a::after { display: none }' then 1767 'a[href^=http]::after { display: inline }'. Works today due to selector specificity + source order but the two rules read contradictory. A future edit inserting between them could accidentally break URL-in-print. Fix: scope the suppression to 'a:not([href^=http])::after { display: none }' — intent becomes self-documenting.

title: .skip-link uses :focus not :focus-visible — asymmetric outline semantics
description: src/global.css:1136 uses '.skip-link:focus { top: 0 }' to reveal the skip link, but the global focus ring rule at line 1142 only applies to :focus-visible. Result: keyboard users see link+outline (both fire), mouse users see link positioned but no outline. Minor asymmetry. Fix: add explicit outline in .skip-link:focus-visible block so the ring is not cascade-dependent.

title: storage event handler ignores newValue === null (cross-tab removeItem)
description:
src/global.client.js storage listener (~lines 117-121) filters 'typeof e.newValue === string' which correctly excludes null. But this means if another tab calls localStorage.removeItem('theme'), the current tab's data-theme attribute is never cleared — stays on last explicit mode instead of reverting to system. Fix: change guard to 'if (e.key === STORAGE_KEY)' and call applyTheme(e.newValue ?? 'system'). See BM One-Shot State Antipattern subtype 3.



## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open site in two tabs (A and B) with an explicit theme set (light or dark).
2. In tab A: localStorage.removeItem('theme').
3. In tab B: the storage event fires with newValue === null.
4. Current handler's typeof e.newValue === 'string' guard skips the null case — tab B retains stale theme instead of reverting to system.
acceptance_criteria: storage event handler treats newValue === null as removal and calls applyTheme('system'); cross-tab localStorage.removeItem('theme') resets the receiving tab to system default; unit/E2E coverage added

title: Console error: Unexpected token ampersand
description: Browser-sync dev server artifact — the '&' in bunny.net font URL is correctly HTML-encoded as & in attributes, but browser-sync's injection script may misparse it. Not present in production builds. Downgraded to P4 (backlog).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] No 'Unexpected token ampersand' console error on page load
- [ ] Root cause identified and fixed
close_reason: Not a code bug. The built HTML correctly encodes & as & in the font URL attribute (public/index.html line 19). This is required by the HTML spec for ampersands in attribute values. Browsers parse it back to & when fetching the URL. The console error is a browser-sync dev server artifact — its script injection misparses the & entity. Production builds are unaffected.
